WPCRL No. 576 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Mohd. Safdar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Ms. Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief 
Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Vaibhav Singh Chauhan, learned 
counsel put appearance on behalf of the 
complainant.
4. Put up this matter on 27.04.2026 as fresh.
5. In the meantime, the State may get 
complete instructions about the past history of 
the petitioner as well as the 
respondent/complainant since both of them are 
from the different place, i.e., Punjab and 
Rajasthan and also get status of the 
investigation. The complainant also file its 
response giving details of the amount of Rs. 9.10 
crore.
7. Mr. H.M. Bhatia, the counsel for the 
Income Tax Department may also get the details 
of both the parties. Mr. Safdar, learned counsel 
for the petitioner shall provide PAN card of the 
petitioner and counsel for the complainant shall 
also provide PAN card of the complainant 
during course of the day to Mr. Bhatia.
8. Registry is directed to shown the name of 
Mr. H.M. Bhatia, who is a panel lawyer of 
Income Tax Department in the next cause list as 
an Amicus Curiae in order to assist this court.
9. List this matter on 27.04.2026.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPCRL No. 576 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Mohd. Safdar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, learned counsel for the 
Income Tax Department.
3. Mr. Rajendra Singh Azad, learned counsel for the 
applicant through V.C. in the connected application.
4. Mrs. Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder 
for the State
5. Mr. Shivam Gulati, learned counsel holding the 
brief of Mr. Vaibhav Singh Chauhan, learned counsel 
for the complainant.
6. In compliance of the previous order dated 
24.02.2026 Mr. H.M. Bhatia, learned counsel for the 
Income Tax Department get the income tax details of 
Kulwinder Singh and Somlal Goyal, the respondent in 
WPCRL No. 576 of 2026 and submits that though there 
is a huge transaction in between both of them but the 
same does not reflect from the ITR. The additional 
affidavit has been filed by the respondent no. 3 Mr. 
Somlal. In paragraph 2 and 3 he has given the reference 
of the amount of Rs. 9,60,000/-, however, the learned 
counsel makes a statement that it is a typographical 
mistake and infact the actual amount is Rupees Nine 
crore Sixty lakhs, the copy of which has been supplied 
to Mr. Bhatia in order to enable him to get further 
instructions from the Income Tax officials and to verify 
the amount.
7. Prima-facie it appears that both the parties are 
indulged in transaction of the huge amount but 
deliberately they are not disclosing all those 
transactions in their income tax return and, therefore, 
in view of the judgment of the Hon’ble Apex Court in 
the case of The Correspondence, RBANMS 
Educational Institution vs. B. Gunashekar and 
Another 2025 INSC 490 let the Income Tax Department
may verify and submit their report.
8. Both the parties are agreed to transfer the land. If they want they can proceed.
9. Put up this matter on 13.05.2026.
10. In the meantime, no coercive action shall be taken 
against the applicants/petitioners provided they 
cooperate with the investigation as well as cooperate 
with the income tax officials of the Income Tax 
Department.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 30.04.2026
PR

Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.,
 Mr. Rajendra Singh Azad, learned counsel for the 
applicant through video conferencing in ABA No. 138 of 
2026, Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, learned Amicus Curiae for 
the petitioner in WPCRL No. 576 of 2026 and Mr. Harsh 
Vardhan Dhanik, learned counsel for the petitioner in 
WPCRL No. 1046 of 2026.
2. Mr. Dinesh Chauhan, learned A.G.A. for the State 
of Uttarakhand. 
3. Mr. Vaibhav Singh Chauhan, learned counsel for 
the complainant.
4. Learned State Counsel submits that, during the 
course of investigation, certain additional penal 
provisions have been invoked. He further submits that 
it has come to light that petitioner No. 1- Kulwinder 
Singh, was also arrested in a criminal case in the State 
of Punjab.
5. Mr. H.M. Bhatia, learned counsel, submits that 
pursuant to the order dated 30.04.2026 passed by this 
Court in WP(Crl.) No. 576 of 2026, the concerned 
department is conducting an inquiry into the matter and 
seeks four weeks' further time to place the report on 
record.
6. Learned State Counsel further submits that certain 
subsequent developments have taken place and seeks 
permission to bring the same on record by way of an 
additional affidavit.
7. Permission, as prayed for, is granted.
8. List these cases on 17.07.2026.

Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Sr. Advocate, 
assisted by Ms. Devanshi Joshi, Advocate for 
the applicant in ABA No. 138 of 2026. Mr. 
H.M. Bhatia, Amicus Curiae for the petitioner 
in WPCRL No. 576 of 2026. Mr. Junaid Alam, 
Advocate for the petitioner in WPCRL No. 
1046 of 2026 and Mr. Akshay Pradhan, 
Advocate for the petitioner in WPCRL No. 
1148 of 2026.
2. Mr. Akshay Latwal, A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the 
complainant.
4. Vide order dated 30.04.2026, the 
Coordinate Bench of this Court had directed 
Mr. H.M. Bhatia, learned counsel to 
investigate about the cash transactions, 
which have been alleged in the affidavit filed 
by the complainant.
5. Today, Mr. H.M. Bhatia, learned counsel 
has supplied the report before this Court. The 
same is placed on record. He has submitted 
that Income Tax Department is still  investigating the matter regarding the persons 
residing in the State of Rajasthan and the 
report is expected to be received within two 
weeks.
6. Learned State Counsel prays for and is 
granted further two weeks time to comply with 
the order dated 17.07.2026.
7. List this matter on 23.09.2026.
8. Interim order, if any, to continue till 
then.
